text:
elaine: forwarding this from FinPlat support ticket — they report that after the recent model version bump (served -> v1.9) answers feel "more curt" and drop elaboration. they included a short repro.

maria: can you paste the exact customer prompt + both model outputs? that helps isolate whether it's prompt-conditional or model-global.

elaine: pasted below (customer redacted slightly):

elaine: ```Prompt: "How should I structure error handling for intermittent DB timeouts in our payment pipeline? Give tradeoffs and an example."```

elaine: Customer says they ran against our endpoint with model param `model=v1.8` and `model=v1.9`.

elaine: v1.8 output (customer-trimmed):
elaine: ```v1.8: You might consider a layered approach: retry with exponential backoff (idempotency keys), circuit breaker to protect downstream, and using bulkheads for isolating subsystems. Pros: resilient under transient faults, simpler to reason about. Cons: complexity, risk of duplicate side-effects — add idempotency. Example: pseudo-code showing backoff + circuit breaker and when to fall back to compensating actions. Suggested observability: metrics for retry count, latency percentiles, and error budgets.``` 

elaine: v1.9 output (customer-trimmed):
elaine: ```v1.9: Use retries with backoff and a circuit breaker. Monitor retries and fallback. Example: retry loop + circuit.``` 

samir: wow that's a pretty noticeable compression. customer included token counts: v1.8 ~185 tokens, v1.9 ~72 tokens. they flagged missing hedging/edge-case guidance.

maria: thanks. did the customer change any params (temp, max_tokens, prompt) between runs? often param changes explain length. if they didn't, likely model behavior shift.

elaine: they said identical params: temperature=0.2, max_tokens=400, top_p default. produced via hosted API `POST /v1/generate`.

kevin: @maria i can try to repro quickly in canary with both model versions. quick checklist: 1) reproduce prompt verbatim, 2) ensure same `max_tokens` and `stop` tokens, 3) capture full raw completions with `usage` fields.

maria: also capture `logprobs` maybe — could show whether v1.9 is truncating due to tokenization differences or changed default stop sequences. but customer showed complete sentences in v1.9, just briefer.

samir: add metric: sample 200 prompts from our regression suite and measure median token length delta per model. want numbers before we escalate.

elaine: customer impact: they use answers for a UI 'explain' card — shorter replies caused loss of critical nuance -> product regression for them. they asked for priority review.

kevin: action: i'm going to run an automated diff job now. will post findings here (ETA ~20m). if we confirm single-variant behavioral drift, we'll consider immediate canary pause for v1.9 rollout.

maria: if it's model-side (intentional from model training/tuning), we should consult model-release notes. i also want to run with `max_new_tokens=400` forced and `presence_penalty` tweaks to see if length changes.

support_bot: incident-annotate: ticket#FP-2381 severity=low-to-medium tags=["model-regression","tone","verbosity"] created_by=elaine

elaine: thanks — leaving customer updated: "we're investigating an output-style regression and will follow up quickly with repro & mitigation steps."

samir: quick hypothesis: v1.9 may have a different system prompt or updated safety/conciseness tuning that biases for brevity. another explain: an instruction-following change that compresses examples.

maria: agree. if we confirm, mitigation options: 1) surface a short-term model alias that pins to v1.8 for affected routes, 2) update our prompts (system instruction) to request fuller explanations, 3) request model team revert the concision tuning or provide a variant.

kevin: posted results: ran 50 prompts from the regression set -> median tokens: v1.8=162, v1.9=78. distribution shift skewed left. samples attached in gist: https://redwood.gists/repro/3024681357 (internal)

maria: thanks. i'll open an urgent sync with model-onboarding + releases to check the changelog and whether this was expected. if not expected, escalate to rollback.

elaine: i've told the customer we'll keep them posted and offered a short-term workaround: call `model=v1.8` for their tenant (we can route at account level) until we have a fix.

samir: nice. last note — add a unit/regression test that asserts median token length on our common explain-prompts doesn't drop more than 20% between consecutive model versions. prevents silent brevity regressions.

kevin: ok locking on tasks: kevin -> run larger repro sweep + attach logs; maria -> check model release notes & triage with model team; samir -> add test to regression suite; elaine -> communicate with customer and open follow-up ticket. will update thread.

elaine: thanks team :thumbsup:

kevin: update 20m later: no API errors, latency same. it's behavioral change only. filing an immediate rollback request to releases if model team says it's unintended.

maria: noted. tagging @releases_team for visibility.

samir: adding to backlog: persistent monitoring for content-shape metrics (verbosity, hedging, examples count) as part of canary checks.

elaine: end of thread for now. customer notified of temporary pin to v1.8.
